title: UAV Trajectory Optimization for Aerial Surveying
description: Develop and validate trajectory optimization methods for small uncrewed aerial vehicles performing terrain survey missions. The student will formulate waypoint and continuous-time optimal control problems, implement them in MATLAB, and verify resulting flight paths in a Gazebo simulation before flight-testing on the lab's quadrotor platform. Emphasis on energy-optimal routing under wind disturbance and on producing reproducible simulation results.
skills: UAV; trajectory optimization; optimal control; waypoint planning; quadrotor; aerial survey; MATLAB; Gazebo; flight path; guidance and control

title: Embedded IoT Sensor Nodes for Precision Irrigation
description: Design battery-powered embedded sensor nodes that measure soil moisture and transmit readings from agricultural test plots. Work includes writing embedded C firmware for ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers, bringing up I2C and SPI sensor drivers under an RTOS, laying out a low-power PCB, and tuning duty cycles so nodes survive a full growing season on primary cells. Field deployment alongside Biological Systems Engineering collaborators.
skills: embedded C; firmware; ARM Cortex-M; microcontroller; RTOS; I2C; SPI; sensor driver; PCB design; low-power; soil moisture; LoRaWAN

title: Research Computing Infrastructure and Linux Systems Administration
description: Maintain the systems that support a research group's experiments: Debian servers, a Proxmox virtualization cluster, ZFS storage with snapshot replication, and containerized workloads. The student will write Ansible roles to make configuration reproducible, author systemd units for lab services, manage VLANs and firewall rules, and build Prometheus and Grafana dashboards so failures are caught before deadlines are missed. Includes a documented backup and restore drill.
skills: Linux; systems administration; Debian; Bash; Ansible; systemd; Proxmox; ZFS; Docker; networking; VLAN; Prometheus; backup; uptime

title: Undergraduate Teaching Assistant - First-Year Engineering (ENGE 1215)
description: Support instruction in the first-year engineering design sequence. Duties include leading MATLAB lab sections for roughly 25 students, holding weekly office hours, grading design notebooks against a rubric, and coaching student teams through open-ended design projects. Successful applicants are patient, communicate clearly to students with no prior programming background, and can give feedback that improves work without discouraging beginners.
skills: teaching assistant; first-year engineering; ENGE 1215; MATLAB; grading; rubric; office hours; mentoring; design notebooks; instruction; communication

title: Full-Stack Developer - Campus Sustainability Dashboard
description: Build the public web application that reports campus energy and emissions data. The stack is React with TypeScript on the front end and Node.js with PostgreSQL behind a REST API. The student will implement interactive data visualizations, wire up Docker Compose and GitHub Actions for continuous integration and deployment, and meet WCAG accessibility requirements so the dashboard is usable with a screen reader.
skills: React; TypeScript; Node.js; PostgreSQL; REST API; full-stack; Docker; CI/CD; GitHub Actions; accessibility; WCAG; data visualization; responsive design
